t.E472b.agn: In 2020 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern at the reported use levels.
t.E472b.body: During digestion in the body it is largely broken down into glycerol, fatty acids and the corresponding organic acid (lactic acid); these are used like the fats in foods.
t.E472b.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E472b.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by esterification of glycerol with lactic acid and fatty acids or by reaction of mono- and diglycerides with lactic acid.
t.E472b.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern.
t.E472b.regx.1: Specifications follow-up opinion: changes to the EU specifications recommended for E472b.
t.E472b.summary: An emulsifier derived from mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids. It improves texture in bread, cake and margarine; the fat source may be vegetable or animal.
t.E472b.what: As an emulsifier, it improves foam and consistency.
